newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fuji Heavy says will not up 96/97 profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Fuji Heavy says will not up 96/97 profit forecast.

text.p: Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd has no plans to raise its profit forecast for the current 1996/97 fiscal year, a company spokesman said on Monday.
The Asian Wall Street Journal reported on Monday that Fuji Heavy"s profits would be better than expected for the year ending in March as a result of the weaker yen.
"We don"t expect a weaker yen to increase our profits for 1996/97 because we see an increase in appraisal losses for our securities holdings and other higher expenditure," the spokesman said.
In November, Fuji Heavy, owned 4.2 percent by Nissan Motor Co Ltd, forecast parent current profits of 26 billion yen in the year to March 1997, up from 10.11 billion a year earlier.
Fuji Heavy's share price rose 19 yen to 559 in the Tokyo morning session.
